name: Iron Albatross (Wide Iron Condor)
summary: An iron condor with very far OTM short strikes (5-8 delta) and wide wings - a high-probability, low-credit tail-selling structure.

legs.strike_rule: short put minus wing width W (W >= 2x the strike increment; typically $10 on SPY)
short call plus the same wing width W

max_loss: (W - net credit) x 100 (large relative to the credit)
breakevens: short put - credit; short call + credit

greeks.gamma: negative, very small until a tail event
greeks.theta: positive but small in absolute terms

when_to_use: IV rank >= 40 with a steep volatility skew that makes far-OTM puts rich. It is a tail-selling trade: high win rate, occasional large loss. Only run it with strict sizing.
entry_rules: Net credit >= 12% of the wing width W (far-OTM credit is thin; below this the risk/reward is indefensible)
Short strikes at 0.05-0.08 delta both sides
Max loss <= 1% of equity per position AND total albatross max loss <= 5% of equity across all positions
No earnings or macro binary inside the expiry
Far-OTM strikes still need OI >= 250 and a quotable bid (a wing you cannot sell is not a wing)
management_rules: Take profit at 50% of credit, or at 21 DTE, whichever first
Loss stop: close if the buy-back cost >= 3x the credit received (the loss multiple must be larger than an iron condor's because the credit is small relative to the width)
If either short's delta reaches 0.20, close the whole structure - do not roll a tail trade toward the money
Never add size after a win streak; the payoff distribution is negatively skewed by design
exit_rules: Force-close by 15:45 ET on expiration day, always
Close immediately if any short strike is breached intraday (spot beyond the short strike) regardless of the model price
Close if a short leg's extrinsic < $0.10 or delta >= 0.85
Ex-dividend guard on the short call
assignment_risk: Low frequency, high severity: the shorts are far OTM most of the time, but a gap through a short strike leaves an ITM short with real assignment exposure. The close-on-breach rule exists for this.
buying_power: (W - credit) x 100 per contract - capital-inefficient relative to the credit collected.
liquidity_needs: Far-OTM strikes are often wide; require a two-sided quote with spread <= $0.10 and OI >= 250 on every leg.
common_mistakes: Treating a 95% win rate as a strategy; oversizing because 'it never gets tested'; wings so wide the single loss erases a year of credits; strikes so far out the bid is $0.01 and slippage eats everything.
zero_dte_notes: Not recommended. 0DTE far-OTM credits are a few cents while a single intraday breach costs the full width; the risk/reward is indefensible and slippage alone exceeds the edge.
family: four-leg structures (iron condors, iron butterflies, condors, double calendars/diagonals, boxes, jelly rolls, conversions/reversals, double verticals, double ratio spreads)
